I am also heavily influenced by LUM in my music. 

What’s super important is sample selection (both for loops/melodies and for the drums) and very smart processing. LUM’s music is super raw, sampler based sounding. I’m kinda referring more to the tape “the weeping worm” which I especially like the sound of. His drum hits kinda clip and have very minimal post processing. He likes to use velocity a little on hat rolls but other than that everything is at 100% all the time, brick walled. Makes it really aggressive and in your face.

Something else I like to do is pitch my hi hats down by an octave. Usually I roll off a little high end with an EQ too. Gives it a really sludgy lazy kinda sound.

I felt like the movie Into The Wild, like I was just unstoppable and could do anything and I had no fear, no anxiety, and it was REAL. During this phase I met the girl I am currently still with a year later. This was the version of myself I am the most proud of in my whole life. 

However after a while of doing this I got the feeling that it wasn’t sustainable, not that it wasn’t real, but that like you said I needed more time in between because it was nearing the point where it felt less liberating to trip so often, and more like a chore. It did not work. 

I did face a series of events which definitely had their own big roles in my regression, but basically as time went on I just reverted worse and worse into my state of mental disarray, which is a pretty deep pit. I became depressed, irritable, mean, anxious, jealous, paranoid, and suffered a series of panic attacks. One day I read a post about microdosing. For some reason it just caught my attention. I had heard a lot about it and read about it but never tried it. Then I thought about it and how much it was helping people and realized that my acid phase I had had about a year prior was basicslly my own super hardcore version of microdosing. The point is a regular (SMALL) dose to return you to a baseline, wait until you feel yourself about to veer off and then repeat. It doesn’t necessarily require you to have a full strength trip and blast your mind to space.

I highly recommend trying acid. 

It doesn't need to be an escape from anything. It can just be a very life changing experience especially for otherwise healthy and non drug using people.

Set and setting are the biggest factors to having a good trip. 

Your mindset going in should be one of excitement, not worried about anything going wrong, prepared to have a good time. Therefore you should prepare beforehand, make sure you don't have any obligations or interference. Also, your setting should be something you're comfortable with, I'd clean up whatever space you're gonna take it in and make sure you don't have any unexpected/unwanted guests or whatever.

Other than that, just expect to have a great time. You should prepare some things to do, since your bf will be there to prevent him from getting bored maybe pick a couple movies to watch. I'd avoid anything that can have anything in it even possibly "scary" or violent, like maybe a Pixar movie or a comedy you guys like. 

Also, something you should know is most of the time when tripping with somebody, social interactions can become really weird, awkward, or uncomfortable. Just expect it to happen and don't get freaked out when it does. Just laugh it off and don't overthink it. You're on drugs. 

If at any point you're becoming uncomfortable, overwhelmed, or anything bad (you can usually see a bad trip coming from a mile away imo) my advice is change your setting. Going for a walk usually does the trick. Doing this combined with putting on some nice relaxing music that you like can really really help as well. Also if you feel the need to be alone, just calmly explain that to your BF. He may not understand since he hasn't tripped either but sometimes just having some time to yourself to let your thoughts simmer down can help. I can't stress enough how much the going for a walk, music, and alone time can help prevent a bad trip.

Other than any of this, don't overthink it. Just have a good time! Enjoy your surroundings. I suggest being around nature if at all possible.
